notes_for_editor: Thin record and possibly a non-tower entry. Both lookout sources name the site and county only; no build, staffing, fire, fate or access source was found, so the story says nothing about those. Elevation differs: the tower list gives 1,349 with no unit stated, so the record's 411.2 m assumes feet, which the list does not say; MountainZone gives an approximate 1,329 ft (405 m) for the summit. The story gives the list figure with no unit and MountainZone's figure with its unit, and the record was not changed. Unread lead, not used: a Facebook post on the Douglas County GA History page (https://www.facebook.com/DouglasCountyGAHistory/posts/this-towering-structure-remembered-locally-as-a-fire-beacon-once-stood-in-the-bi/1508695837928675/) says a 'Fire Beacon' tower once stood in the Bill Arp section of Douglas County and was dismantled in the 1950s. Only a search snippet was read (it is cut off mid-sentence), so it may or may not be this site; a human should check it. Record kind 'tower', agency and status are not confirmed by any source read.
